_meta.what_this_is: Two tool schemas and six tool calls a model proposed. Each schema lists the tool's required arguments and their types. Each call names a tool and supplies arguments. One call is well-formed; the other five are each malformed in a different way -- an unknown tool, a missing required argument, two wrong-type arguments, and an unexpected extra argument -- exactly the ways a model's structured output goes wrong. A validating harness checks each call against its schema and rejects the malformed ones before executing.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The schemas and calls are hand-authored so the one valid call and the five distinct rejection reasons are exact and checkable; every validation is computed in validate.py. Note booleans are rejected where an int is required (a common trap, since bool is a subclass of int in Python).
_meta.format: schemas: {tool: {param: type}} with types str/int/bool/float; calls: [{id, tool, args}].
